core_meaning.primary_meaning: Abasi represents Arabic عباسي (ʿAbbāsī), a nisba adjective meaning related to or associated with ʿAbbās; it does not literally mean “servant of Abbas.”
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Arabic عباسي is a nisba adjective formed from the name ʿAbbās and can mean belonging to, associated with, or descended from a person/family called ʿAbbās. It is also associated historically with the Abbasid dynasty. The previous translation “servant of Abbas” was inaccurate.

etymology.morphology: Nisba adjective formed from عباس (ʿAbbās) with the relational suffix ـي.
etymology.etymology_explanation: عباسي is a relational adjective (nisba) associated with عباس, used for affiliation or relation; it does not mean عبد العباس (“servant of al-ʿAbbās”).
etymology.false_etymology_warning: No derivation beyond the documented Arabic form is asserted. Any etymology that attributes this spelling to a different root or language without a source should be treated as unverified.

faq.a: Abasi represents Arabic عباسي (ʿAbbāsī), meaning related to or associated with ʿAbbās.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abasi?
faq.a: The recorded form عباسي is Arabic and is a relational adjective (nisba).
Yes. The underlying Arabic form is عباسي (ʿAbbāsī).

faq.q: What is the root of Abasi?
faq.a: The form is derived relationally from عباس with the nisba suffix ـي; no separate root analysis is asserted here.
Abasi can function as a family/relational name in Muslim contexts, but it does not literally mean “servant of Abbas.”
This record does not establish Abasi as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin alone is not proof of scriptural status.

faq.q: What does Abasi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written عباسی and means related to or associated with Abbas, not “عباس کا بندہ.”
The supplied “a-ba-si” is an approximate romanization of عباسي (ʿAbbāsī).

faq.q: Is Abasi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Abasi as masculine, but usage as a given name versus surname can vary by community.
